newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads Dole by 12.6 percent in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads Dole by 12.6 percent in Reuters poll.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent
President Bill Clinton led Republican challenger Bob Dole by 12.6 percentage points in the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Tuesday, while the battle for control of Congress remained tight.

Clinton scored 45.5 percent to Dole's 32.9 percent in the poll conducted by John Zogby Group International, which had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.2 percentage points. The survey included around 1,100 likely voters interviewed between Saturday and Monday.
The poll showed Reform Party candidate Ross Perot edging up to 8.3 percent while 10.7 percent of respondents were still undecided with only one week to go until Election Day Nov 5.
"This race is beginning a narrowing down and should ultimately move into a single-digit margin," pollster John Zogby said. Three key questions to watch in the final week of the campaign were:
-- Whether Clinton achieves 50 percent, giving him a clear mandate in a second term.
-- Whether his lead reaches 13 percent or more, which would enhance the possibility of a Democratic Congress.
-- Whether Perot reaches 10 percent, which might help bring out a Republican congressional vote, since more Perot voters lean Republican in congressional races.

When asked whom they would vote for in their congressional districts, 39.1 percent said they would back Democrats compared to 36.5 percent for Republicans. But polls in past elections have somewhat overestimated the Democratic vote, especially in elections where the turnout is relatively low as this year's may be.
When they were asked which party they would prefer to see in the majority in the Senate and the House of Representatives, slight majorities opted for the Republicans.
But Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich was viewed negatively by two out of three voters, while only one in four gave him as positive job rating.
